column_name: what predicts activity? (e.g. accessible -> active in MPRA?)
proposed_value: Chromatin accessibility (DNase I hypersensitivity), H3K27ac levels, and binding of activating transcription factors such as AP-1 (JUN and ATF3) strongly correlate with enhancer activity in ExP STARR-seq, with E1-class enhancers showing significantly higher levels of these features compared to E2-class enhancers. Additionally, ETS-family motifs (e.g., GABPA) are positively correlated with enhancer activity but negatively correlated with enhancer responsiveness, suggesting a tuning role in enhancer-promoter compatibility.
rationale:
- E1 sequences showed stronger associations with H3K27ac, DNase I hypersensitivity, and AP-1 factor binding compared to E2 sequences (Fig. 3a, Extended Data Fig. 6a-d). 
- Enhancer activity in ExP STARR-seq correlated with biochemical features including chromatin accessibility, H3K27ac, and nascent RNA transcription (Extended Data Fig. 1g). 
- ETS-family motifs (e.g., GABPA) were positively correlated with enhancer activity but negatively correlated with responsiveness, indicating a regulatory tuning role (page 8).
